主要内容: Reynolds American, a major tobacco company, has entered into a $27 billion merger with Lorillard, a smaller competitor. This deal includes the sale of Lorillard's Blu e-cig brand to Imperial Tobacco Group for $7.1 billion. The merger is significant as it marks the first time a Big Three tobacco company has entered the e-cig market. Lorillard acquired Blu in 2012, and it has since become the leading brand in the fast-growing $2 billion nicotine vapor space. Reynolds American has decided to retain its own e-cig brand, Vuse, as the sole e-cig brand in the merged company. The decision to sell Blu to Imperial Tobacco Group may have been influenced by the involvement of British American Tobacco, which owns about 42% of Reynolds and has agreed to buy additional shares to finance the merger. Analysts suggest that British American Tobacco may not want to compete with itself in the U.K. market, where Blu operates. In a major tobacco deal, e-cig company Blu was spun off to Imperial Tobacco, a move that may have been aimed at easing antitrust concerns. The sale of Blu, along with Reynolds' menthol brands Kool and Salem, was part of a larger deal. Antitrust regulators were more concerned about the menthol brands than the e-cig brands, as Blu's small market size made it less of a concern. Imperial Tobacco insisted on acquiring Blu, while Reynolds felt it was not necessary. The change in ownership of Blu is unlikely to affect Logic's sales, as the brand continues to face competition from Logic and ongoing industry disruption. Companies like Logic, which do not sell traditional combustible tobacco products, may have an advantage in shelf space due to convenience stores keeping a larger percentage of the sale price with their products. Additionally, Blu faces competition from open system vaping devices, which allow users to refill devices with their chosen nicotine liquid.
